changes_vs_current: Out (13): Mad Men, Succession, West Wing, Lost, Friday Night Lights, Six Feet Under, Leftovers, Deadwood, Severance, The Crown, Yellowstone, Ozark, House of the Dragon; In (13): Sherlock, The Pitt, Grey's Anatomy, Black Mirror, The Boys, Dexter, Walking Dead, Battlestar Galactica, Law & Order, Twilight Zone, Bridgerton, Fargo, Dark; Stranger Things moves from #12 to #3.
confidence: low-medium. Top 4 (GoT, Breaking Bad, Stranger Things, Sopranos) pass the party test, but only 3 people-sources exist and the math is IMDb-heavy. IMDb skews young, male and international, which lifts Sherlock (#5), Peaky Blinders, Black Mirror, Dark and True Detective over shows Americans watch more (Yellowstone averages 21.7 and misses the cut; Lost 18.2, Succession 18.2, West Wing 18.0, Criminal Minds 17.3 and Narcos/Squid Game 17.5 are bunched just outside). The Pitt (#6) is a 2025 show and may be too recent. Positions 14-24 sit within 1.5 points and each rests on a single source. YouGov Ratings no longer has a TV-drama page (404); its all-time and current TV pages (top 20 only) are dominated by cartoons, game shows and procedurals, so I did not use them. No Harris, Morning Consult or Talker drama poll newer than 2022 turned up. Ranker blocked.
